environment.observed_identity: Turso (Rust SQLite rewrite), SQL compatibility 3.50.4; journal_mode=wal; synchronous=FULL; busy_timeout=5000ms
environment.client_transport: turso crate, one embedded async connection per concurrency slot driven through a current-thread runtime, connection-cached statement per operation, autocommit per statement

comparability.seed_policy: seed-{index}, tenant benchmark-tenant, index modulo seed count
comparability.document_policy: seed documents have id seed-{index}, name user-{index}, group index modulo 100, 256-byte payload
comparability.operation_policy: mixed uses index modulo 10: 0..4 read, 5..7 write, 8..9 query; read/query address index modulo seed count
comparability.write_id_policy: measured writes use measured-{global operation index}
comparability.durability_semantics: WAL journal with synchronous=FULL and a five-second busy timeout; autocommit statement acknowledgement
comparability.server_configuration_provenance: turso crate at shipped defaults plus WAL, synchronous=FULL, busy_timeout=5000ms

limits: embedded reference: the measured member is this driver's own process, so the load generator and the database share one resource envelope
the engine's native Rust API is async: each slot drives its connection through its own current-thread runtime with block_on per operation, so per-operation latencies include that boundary

sixteen per-slot writers contend through turso's MVCC: stale-snapshot and busy conflicts are retried per turso's documented pattern, bounded by a 30-second per-operation deadline, and every retry's wait is part of the measured latency
